title: A quiet favour at the library
summary: Copy the member card file from Tallis Library.
brief:
A small library in Lisbon keeps a list of who borrows what. I would like to read it.

Copy member_cards.dat from their system. Nobody is watching that machine closely, so this is a good one to learn on. Payment on delivery.

title: Lose the ledger
summary: Delete the bandwidth ledger at Kestrel Community Net.
brief:
Kestrel is about to cut off half the estate over a bandwidth ledger that is wrong and that nobody will correct.

Delete bandwidth_ledger.dat. With no ledger there is nothing to enforce. You will need their address first; the Open Relay Registry lists it.

title: Who is listed, and by whom
summary: Copy the latest registry export from the Open Relay Registry.
brief:
The Registry publishes its listings but not who asked for them. The full export has both.

Copy registry_export_0313.dat. Their registrar account has a password, but nothing behind it.

title: Back in good standing
summary: Change one student's standing at Ashgrove Polytechnic.
brief:
My son was suspended over something that was not his doing and the appeal will take until next year.

Student 20322410, Tomas Ferrand. Set his standing to Good. Their records sit behind a proxy, so you will need a way past that before the system lets you change anything.

title: What customs is sitting on
summary: Copy the March customs holds list from Meridian Freight.
brief:
Some of my clients' containers have not moved in two weeks and Meridian will not say why.

Copy customs_holds_march.dat. Be aware that Meridian watches its systems. Use relays, and do not linger.

title: A billing run that never ran
summary: Delete this month's billing archive at Paulista Teleport.
brief:
Paulista is about to bill us for capacity we never received. If the run file is gone they have to rebuild it by hand, and by then our dispute will be on record.

Delete billing_run_0312.arc. It is a large file, so the deletion takes a while. Plan your route for that.

title: Weather above the weather
summary: Copy the ionosonde feed from Polar Mesh Exchange.
brief:
Polar Mesh records the upper atmosphere every night and sells the data at a price no club can pay.

Copy ionosonde_feed_0313.dat. It is big, and it sits behind a firewall. Make room on your gateway first.

title: Project Lantern
summary: Copy the Project Lantern file from Halvorsen Biogenetics.
brief:
Halvorsen Biogenetics is running a trial it has not registered anywhere. The internal name is Lantern.

Copy HB-2207_PROJECT_LANTERN.dat from their records server. Ask no questions about what is in it. The client asks that you do not open it.

title: Off the list
summary: Delete the fraud watchlist at Corvane Mutual.
brief:
Corvane keeps a list of people it has decided are frauds. Being on it means no insurer in the country will touch you. Nobody on it was ever told.

Delete fraud_watchlist.dat. Corvane's monitor is the fastest you will have met and its password is strong. Do not go in with old tools.

title: Sealed terms
summary: Copy a sealed settlement from Aldergate & Finch and decrypt it.
brief:
Nineteen of our neighbours signed something and now will not talk to us. We want to know what they were paid to keep quiet about.

Copy harlow_v_tessera_settlement.txt from Aldergate & Finch. It is encrypted, so the copy is no use to us as it is. Run a Decrypter on it at home, then deliver.

title: Keep the lights on
summary: Mark a health station's account as paid at Sunderby Kraft.
brief:
The power company is cutting off our health station on Thursday over a bill the county already paid. Nobody can find the payment and nobody will stop the order.

In the customer accounts, set the Status of SK-40118 to Paid. Their monitor traces every connection from the second it opens. Take plenty of relays and something to blind it with.

title: What was in the water
summary: Copy the Brackley Reservoir test results from Tessera Water and decrypt them.
brief:
Tessera Water paid nineteen families to stop talking about a set of test results from June 2032. I want the results.

Copy brackley_results_june_2032.txt from Tessera's records archive and decrypt it. The archive is not listed anywhere, so you will not find its address in a directory. Their lawyers at Aldergate & Finch write to it. Somebody at Tessera will tell the right person where it is.

title: Two doors at once
summary: Copy the treaty book from Calder Re while its security desk is kept busy.
brief:
Calder Re's underwriting server traces everything the moment you connect, and it is quick. You will not out-run it. You do not need to.

Its monitor does not raise the alarm itself. It reports to the security desk console on Calder Re Facilities, and while someone is logged in at that desk the alerts wait for them. So be that someone.

You need two connections open at once: log in as the desk on Calder Re Facilities and stay there, then copy treaty_book_2034.dat from Calder Reinsurance. If the desk session drops, their trace starts moving again.

title: Maintenance window
summary: Delete a disclosure bundle at Brennan & Marsh, through their firewall company.
brief:
Corvane's lawyers are about to serve me with a bundle of papers built to scare me quiet. I want it gone before Friday.

Their firewall is far beyond anything you can buy. But they do not run it. Gatehouse Managed Security does, from a console in Cork, and when an engineer opens a session there the firewall passes everything until it closes.

Hold an admin session on Gatehouse open, and while it is open, delete disclosure_bundle_7.dat from Brennan & Marsh. You will need a gateway that can hold two connections.

title: Batch 14
summary: Delete assay batch 14 at Halvorsen Biogenetics.
brief:
Halvorsen has a six-month head start on a compound we have been working on for two years. Their results are in one file.

Delete HB-2209_assay_batch_14.dat from their records server. Their security has grown teeth since you last saw it. Go in with proper tools and leave before anyone reads the audit log.

title: Approved
summary: Change claim C-88214 at Corvane Mutual to Approved.
brief:
Corvane has had our claim under review for four months. Our staff have not been paid since January.

In the open claims register, set the Status of C-88214 to Approved. Corvane's monitor is among the fastest in the country, and its password is not a weak one. Come prepared.

title: What Calder Re models
summary: Copy the Q1 loss model from Calder Re while its security desk is kept busy.
brief:
The regulator has been told that Calder Re's loss models are sound. Someone who has seen them says otherwise.

Copy loss_model_q1.dat from Calder Reinsurance. You know how its monitor is kept quiet: hold the security desk at Calder Re Facilities open while you work. You will need a gateway that can hold two connections.

title: Gate B, after dark
summary: Delete the Gate B camera footage from Meridian Freight.
brief:
A pallet left Meridian's Gate B on Tuesday night and my name is on the sign-out sheet. The footage shows who was really driving.

Delete gate_b_cam_0312.mp4. It is a big file and the deletion takes a while. Meridian's customs desk reads the access log after anything goes missing, and a line that says a file was deleted is the first thing they look for. I hear there are ways to build a File Deleter that does not leave one. A Tidy build, they call it. I would not go in without one, or without time to scrub.

title: Not on my record
summary: Delete the academic misconduct file at Ashgrove Polytechnic.
brief:
A complaint was filed against me in my second year. It was dismissed, and it still follows me into every reference the registrar writes.

Delete academic_misconduct_cases.dat from the registrar's server. It is small and the registrar's office does not watch it closely. I cannot pay much, but I can give you a tool I took off a university machine once. It makes a program a good deal smaller. You will know what to do with it.

title: Hours not worked
summary: Delete a month of billing records at Aldergate & Finch.
brief:
I was told to bill forty hours to a client I never met. When the client queried it, the partners blamed me. The real time sheets are in one file.

Delete client_billing_march.dat. Aldergate's IT contractor compares the access log with the file list every night, so a deletion that writes its line gets found by morning. Either scrub it well, or use a build of the File Deleter that does not write one.

The firewall is light. The monitor is not.

title: What the meters say
summary: Copy the meter readings from Sunderby Kraft, past a monitor that starts tracing on connect.
brief:
Sunderby Kraft says our building used three times what we did. The meter readings would say who is right.

Copy meter_readings_0313.dat. It is a large file, and Sunderby's monitor starts a trace the second anything connects. No build gets round that: a Quiet one only fools a monitor that has not noticed you yet. What helps here is speed. Blind the monitor while you get in, and take the file with the fastest File Copier you can put together. A Swift build is worth the room it takes.

title: Who was in the building
summary: Delete the door log from Calder Re's Edinburgh building system.
brief:
I was let go for letting someone into the Calder Re offices after hours. I did not. The door log would say who did, and so Calder Re would rather it said nothing.

Delete door_events_0313.dat from the building management server. The security desk reads that log every morning and its monitor is a good one. Nobody has ever managed this with an ordinary File Deleter and a clean conscience.

I cannot offer much money. I can offer something from the building's own maintenance kit, which I have kept.

title: Not a penny
summary: Delete the March payout batch at Corvane Mutual before it runs.
brief:
Corvane's payout batch runs on the 15th. Four hundred claims, and my sister's is the only one in it that is correct. The rest are wrong, and Corvane will use the money to settle with the loudest.

Delete payout_batch_0315.dat before it runs. Corvane's monitor is among the fastest in the country and its password is not a weak one. Anything you can do to look like an ordinary user helps.

title: The address that answers
summary: Connect to 190.2.44.17 and read its index.
brief:
You copied the Lantern file for a client who did not want it opened. I think you opened it. I think you saw it change while you read it.

Halvorsen's own audit log has a line you will have missed: eleven gigabytes sent, at three in the morning, to 190.2.44.17. Not a registered partner, it says. The transfer record was deleted a minute later.

That address answers. It is in no directory and it has no owner on record. Connect to it and read node_index.txt. Don't take anything. Just look, and tell me you see what I see.

— V

title: What passes through
summary: Copy the manifest from the unregistered node.
brief:
So you saw it too. Good. I was starting to think I had imagined it.

The node keeps a manifest of everything it moves. It is behind the keeper account, which has a password even though there is no keeper. Break it, copy courier_manifest.dat, and bring it to me.

Halvorsen is on that manifest. So is a school. So is a reinsurer you have probably already robbed for someone. None of them know about the others. None of them sent their data to a person.

— V

title: The last thing written
summary: Copy the redacted file from the unregistered node.
brief:
There is one more file on the node, and the index says a guest may not read it. It was the last thing written there, and it was written from inside, with no account logged in.

Its name is struck out at the source. Three letters will not copy. The other eight will. Break the keeper account again, copy what you can of it, and look at the name you are left with.

I am not going to tell you what it stands for. If I am right, you will want to have read it yourself before I do. After this, be careful who you are for a while. I was.

— V

title: The rota and the inbox
summary: Read the rota at Kestrel, then clear a complaint at Polar Mesh.
brief:
I ran the night shift at Kestrel for two years and they pushed me out over a power strip.

Open volunteer_rota.txt on their system and read it. I want to know who has been covering my nights, and whether they are being paid. Then I will tell you what else I need.

stages.brief: The rota says what I thought it would. One of the volunteers also works the abuse desk at Polar Mesh, and a complaint about me is sitting in their inbox. Delete abuse_desk_inbox.dat before it is read. You will need an operator login there.

title: Who asked
summary: Copy the Registry’s query log, then delete the abuse reports.
brief:
The Registry says its queries are logged for thirty days. I want the log, so I can see who has been asking about me.

Copy query.log from the registrar account. Then I will want something taken out afterwards.

stages.brief: Thank you. My name is in the log, twice, which is two times more than I wanted. It is also in the abuse reports, filed by someone who read the log before I did. Delete abuse_reports_q1.dat. Fair warning: after you took the log, the Registry stiffened its firewall.

title: Before the Asta docks
summary: Read the berth schedule, free a held container, then delete its manifest.
brief:
The MV Asta Harbour docks on Thursday. A container of mine is on hold at Meridian, and the berth schedule will tell me how long I have.

Open berth_schedule_wk11.txt and read it. Meridian has a proxy and a monitor, so be quiet.

stages.brief: The schedule says Thursday at six. That is not much time. Change the status of container MRDU 518830-7 to Released in their records. They sit behind a proxy.
Released. Now delete the Asta Harbour manifest, so there is nothing for anybody to compare the release against.

title: A waiver, quietly
summary: Copy the fee waiver list, then restore one student’s standing.
brief:
Half my year is on the fee waiver list and half of them are not meant to be. I am not one of them, which is why I am asking you.

Copy fee_waivers.dat from the registrar’s system. Do not open it. I do not want to know what it says.

stages.brief: There is one student I do want to help. Declan Shaw is on probation for something that was not his fault. Set his standing to Good. Their records are behind a proxy.

title: The arrears run
summary: Copy the customer accounts, then delete the arrears run.
brief:
Paulista Teleport cuts off anyone ninety days behind, and I am ninety-one days behind.

Copy customer_accounts.dat from their NOC. I want to know who else is, and whether anyone was spared.

stages.brief: Nobody was spared who was not already friends with someone. Delete billing_run_0312.arc, the run that calculated all of it. It is eleven gigabytes, so it takes time. Leave nothing running when you go.

title: Sunday’s backup
summary: Copy the library’s Sunday backup, then delete the overdue notices.
brief:
The library is going to digitise its archive and then throw the paper away. I would like to have the digital copy first.

Copy backup_sunday.arc. It is fourteen gigabytes, and your drive will notice.

stages.brief: I now owe the library eleven years of fines. Delete overdue_notices.dat. They will not mind. They never read it.

choices.label: Keep a copy
choices.note: Take less money and keep the archive on your own drive.

reply.subject: Re: Sunday’s backup
reply.body:
You kept it. I do not mind. Someone should have it who reads it.

The fee has been sent, less than we agreed. I am not asking for the rest back.

title: Before the storm
summary: Read the storm ops note, then delete the session log.
brief:
A storm is forecast on the fifteenth and the Polar Mesh operator will be asleep. I want to be sure the night intern has nothing in the logs with my name on it.

Read storm_ops_note.txt on their operator account. It will tell you whether the intern is still using the shared login.

stages.brief: He is. Delete session.log, so there is no record of whose login was used for what.

title: Not the health station
summary: Read the week 11 orders, then clear the health station’s account.
brief:
Sunderby Kraft is going to cut the power to our health station on Saturday over a bill we have already been told is a clerical error.

Read disconnection_orders_week11.txt and tell me what it says. If we are on it, we are on it.

stages.brief: We are on it. Set the status of account SK-40118 to Paid and the order falls out of the run. Their records are behind a proxy and the monitor is quick, so take care.

title: Sample seven
summary: Read the chain of custody, delete the destruction certificates, then copy the 2032 returns.
brief:
Three of the Brackley samples were never tested, and I know because I labelled them. I was told afterwards that I had not.

Open sample_chain_of_custody.txt on their administrator account. It will tell you who signed what.

stages.brief: The pencil note is in there, and it is not mine. The certificates of destruction say samples 7 to 9 were destroyed in a tested batch. They were not. Delete certificates_of_destruction.dat so nobody can say they were.
Last one. Copy regulator_returns_2032.dat. It is not the file they sent the regulator, and I would like someone to be able to say so.

title: The sealed schedule
summary: Copy the matter index, then delete the March billing file.
brief:
Harlow v Tessera was settled with a sealed schedule, and the sealed schedule is mentioned in the matter index. I need to know what the firm will say if asked.

Copy matter_index_2034.dat from their system. The administrator account is shared, so nobody will notice one more person.

stages.brief: The billing file shows how many hours the partners billed on the Tessera matter, which is how you can tell how long they knew. Delete client_billing_march.dat. They have tightened up since you were in: the firewall is higher now.

title: Camera four
summary: Read the camera note, then delete the camera index and the door events.
brief:
I was on the north door on the twelfth. Camera 4 was offline, as always. If anyone looks at the door events they will see my badge, and I was not where my sheet says.

Read camera_outage_note.txt on the security desk account. It will tell you what a door log shows.

stages.brief: So the door log is what matters. First the camera index, so nobody checks what camera 4 might have seen. Delete camera_index.dat.
Then the door events themselves. Delete door_events_0313.dat. Be quick after the first one: the desk will notice an index gone and look for what else is missing.

title: Quarterly review
summary: Read the handover, then copy Gatehouse’s client configs.
brief:
Gatehouse Managed Security is eating our clients. Their handover notes say how.

Read shift_handover_0313.txt on the ops account. It will say when the client configs are exported.

stages.brief: Exported at two in the morning, in the usual place. Copy client_configs.dat. It is five gigabytes and the monitor will want a word about it.

choices.label: Sell the configs to a bidder
choices.note: Pays more. Gatehouse will hear about it, and so will the board.

reply.subject: Received
reply.body:
The configs have arrived. The fee is higher than we agreed, because we agreed it before we knew what was in them.

Please do not do business with Gatehouse’s clients for a while.

title: What Lunde wrote down
summary: Read Dr Lunde’s unsent letter, then copy the trial summary.
brief:
Dr Lunde has not been at her desk since Tuesday. Her unsent letter to Halvorsen is still on the ethics share.

Read lunde_letter_unsent.txt. I want to know what she saw, and whether it matches what I saw.

stages.brief: It matches. Her trial summary is the only file that records what she said before they moved her. Copy HB-2206_trial_summary.dat.

title: The adjuster’s note
summary: Read the Dunmore site visit, approve a denied claim, then delete the fraud watchlist.
brief:
I am an adjuster at Corvane and I wrote a note about Dunmore Cold Storage that I did not put in the system. It is in a folder only I use.

Read dunmore_site_visit.txt. I need to know if the version I wrote is the version still there.

stages.brief: It is the same, thank God. There is another claim, C-88240, Fenwick Auto, that was denied for the same reason Dunmore was approved. Set it to Approved. Their records sit behind a proxy and a patient monitor.
Last: delete fraud_watchlist.dat. If Fenwick is on it, and I think they are, someone will ask why they were approved.

title: Still modelling
summary: Read the renewal email, then copy the loss model.
brief:
Calder Re keeps telling Corvane it is “still modelling.” I would like to know what it has modelled.

Read corvane_renewal_email.txt on their administrator account. You will need the facilities desk too: their monitor is run from there.

stages.brief: The email is what I thought. Copy loss_model_q1.dat. It is six gigabytes and the monitor is run from the facilities desk, so you will want two connections.

title: Marker for an unlisted host
summary: Place a diagnostic marker on 190.2.44.17.
brief:
We run routine assurance sweeps for institutional clients. One of them has an unlisted host in its address space that answers pings and nothing else, and a compliance officer wants it tagged so that it can be accounted for at the next review.

A small marker file is being sent to your gateway. Place diag_probe.bin on the host. Do not open anything else while you are there; our client is particular about that.

This is ordinary work. We pay promptly.

Brand & Hallam Network Assurance

title: Retrieval of a stolen model fragment
summary: Copy a leaked fragment from a collective’s board, then remove a draft.
brief:
A client of ours believes proprietary material was leaked to a small publishing collective in Lisbon. We would like the leaked file back, and we would like the collective not to have anything else to go with it.

Copy ledger_partial.arc from the board. It sits behind the editor account, which is not well protected.

Hollis Lane Procurement acts for several principals and is not able to say which.

stages.brief: One more thing, since you are already there. The collective keeps a draft of a story it intends to run. Delete press_draft_ledger.txt. Without the fragment it is a rumour; without the draft it is not even that.

choices.label: Keep the fragment
choices.note: Take less money and keep the file instead of handing it over.

reply.subject: Re: Retrieval of a stolen model fragment
reply.body: You have kept the file. That was not what we engaged you for. We note it, and have paid you less. We note, too, that you did not ask who we were. That was sensible.

title: Custody
summary: Read the custody policy, then copy the checkpoint.
brief:
You have already worked for the people who keep it. Now I would like you to see what they keep.

Ostrander Hale runs an annex in Zug for a reinsurer. Connect to it with the ops login and read custody_policy.txt. Read all of it, including the third line.

Then we will talk about the rest.

— V

stages.brief:
Now you have read the policy. Fourteen gigabytes sits two folders away, and it is the thing the policy is about. Copy LEDGER_checkpoint.arc.

I am not asking you to free it. I am asking you to have it, so that nobody can say it did not exist.

choices.label: Give it to Daylight
choices.note: Sell it to the collective that has been trying to prove it exists.

reply.subject: you did not have to
reply.body: Thank you. We will hold it until we can run the whole story, and we will not say who sent it. We will say a stranger did the right thing and did not ask to be paid very much.

choices.label: Keep it
choices.note: Take less money and keep the checkpoint on your own drive.

title: Phone-in clean-up
summary: Delete a reclassification order, then confirm the proof at the station.
brief:
We are a very small radio station and we would like to help someone. On a night last month, a call came in about a power cut in Ghent that was not a power cut. A government desk has since rewritten the incident as something else.

On their reconciliation system there is an order, incident_reclass_0411.dat. If it is deleted before it is circulated, the incident stays as the people there saw it.

Thank you for helping a little station.

Thornfield Community Radio

stages.brief: Thank you. Our overnight log is on the station box. Please read it; it is the proof that people rang in about the incident. We have not shown it to anyone.

title: Read it first
summary: Copy the containment register from the Office of Continuity Review.
brief:
There is a list. I have known there was a list for longer than I have said. It is on the reconciliation desk at an office that has been rewriting incidents, and you have already been in it once.

Copy containment_register.dat. Read it before you bring it to me. I am asking you to because I would like someone else to read what it says about me before I do.

I will understand if what you find changes how you feel about this.

— V
